page: Vultr vc2-6c-16gb is a shared-core cloud instance within the Cloud Compute family, configured with 6 virtual CPUs based on 3 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.0 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture with hyperthreading, the instance supports instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and FMA. It is provisioned with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.67 GB of RAM per vCPU, and includes 320 GB of local NVMe SSD storage along with 1 complimentary public IPv4 address. No dedicated hardware GPUs are attached to this configuration.

Benchmark results demonstrate modest computational throughput typical of shared multi-tenant resources. The single-core Geekbench score of 823.0 and stress-ng single-core performance of 1272.09 place the instance in the lower percentiles for per-thread execution speed, mirrored by low throughput in gzip and bzip3 compression routines. However, aggregate processing scales moderately across its 6 vCPUs, achieving an average stress-ng multi-core score of 6774.42 and sustaining 6.15 million Redis SET operations per second. Uncached read memory bandwidth reaches 48.31 GB/sec, while uncached write bandwidth measures 18.72 GB/sec.

The primary architectural tradeoff of the vc2-6c-16gb is the pairing of entry-level single-thread performance with a generous 320 GB NVMe storage footprint and balanced memory capacity. This combination makes it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that do not demand sustained CPU saturation or rapid sequential processing. Best-fit use cases include staging and test environments, distributed build nodes, background task workers, asynchronous queues, internal tools, and secondary databases or caching layers where local NVMe read and write capacity is advantageous.
description: Vultr vc2-6c-16gb is a Cloud Compute virtual server delivering 6 shared vCPUs on an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz across 3 physical cores. It features 16.0 GB of RAM, 320 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, and a single public IPv4 address without discrete GPU acceleration. The instance exhibits modest single-thread benchmark output, with a Geekbench single-core score of 823.0 and reduced throughput on compression tasks. Nevertheless, multi-threaded tasks achieve steady throughput, illustrated by an average stress-ng multi-core metric of 6774.42 and Redis SET speeds exceeding 6.1 million operations per second. With an advantageous ratio of fast NVMe disk space to shared compute capacity, this server provides a balanced profile for development environments, task processing queues, lightweight web serving, and low-intensity caching databases.
